x: Every feature is open for 14 days, without a card. After that a licence keeps it going.
The top bar shows how long is left: Trial: 14 days left. Click it to open the Licence window.
Your projects still open, and you can keep editing them. Export and AI work need a licence. Nothing you made is lost.

In the Licence window press Buy. The checkout opens in a window of the app and shows the price. When the payment is done, the licence key on the receipt is activated on this computer by itself. The key also comes by email.
Paste your key into Licence key and press Activate. Activated on this computer. confirms it, and the top bar says Licensed.
One licence works on two computers. To use it on a third, free one of them first: open the Licence window there and press Remove This Computer. Then activate the key on the new one.
Kilnframe checks the licence over the internet now and then. If it cannot for 3 weeks, it asks you to connect once.

This key is in use on 2 computers. Remove one of them first. This key was not found. Check it and try again. The subscription has ended. Renew it to export and use AI work again. On Linux, if the key is kept only until you quit, no keyring service is running: start GNOME Keyring or KWallet, then activate again.

t: Use your Claude or ChatGPT plan
x: If you pay for Claude or ChatGPT, Kilnframe can use that plan: the AI work costs nothing extra. It goes through Claude Code or Codex, the companies' own programs on your computer.

t: Use your Claude or ChatGPT plan
x: Claude Plan: Claude Code, the program that runs in the terminal, and a paid Claude plan (Pro, Max, Team or Enterprise). The Claude desktop app is not enough. ChatGPT Plan: Codex, the program that runs in the terminal, signed in with your ChatGPT account. The ChatGPT desktop app is not enough.

t: Use your Claude or ChatGPT plan
x: Open the AI settings Settings › AI › AI Model, and choose Claude Plan or ChatGPT Plan. Install the program, if it is missing The row says not installed and shows the Install command. Press Copy, paste it into Terminal (Command Prompt on Windows), and when it is done press Look Again. Sign in Press Sign In. The program's own sign-in opens in a terminal window; confirm with your account in the browser. It shows up in Kilnframe by itself when done: Signed in, with your plan and the program's version. Pick a model For Claude: Opus 5.5 (recommended), Sonnet 5.5 (faster) or Fable 5.1 (most capable, costs more and is slower). For ChatGPT, Codex's setting uses the model chosen in Codex.

t: Use your Claude or ChatGPT plan
x: Automatic uses your Claude plan when you are signed in, and a Claude API key otherwise.

t: Use your Claude or ChatGPT plan
x: When a new version of Claude Code or Codex is out, the row says update. Old versions can stop working: press Update, and the update runs in a terminal window.

t: Use your Claude or ChatGPT plan
x: The work counts against your Claude or ChatGPT plan, as when you use it yourself. Animations are among the heaviest jobs: the model works on each scene and image separately, and the Animations tab says so before you start. No plan? An API key works too, as do models on your own computer with LM Studio or Ollama.

Kilnframe uses AI in three ways: models that run on your own computer, the AI model you connect for the writing and the judging, and a few services with keys of their own for sound. Nothing goes anywhere you did not choose.

These run on this computer. Nothing is sent and nothing is paid: the transcript (unless you choose cloud transcription); cutting pauses and filler words; finding the person in the frame, to follow them or to put them in front of an animation; voice isolation, noise reduction and echo reduction; finding faces to blur, and searching your footage by a description. Some of them need a model file the first time, such as the 16 MB voice model. It is downloaded only when you start that feature.

The AI model you choose in Settings › AI does the work that needs judgement or writing: finding retakes, asides and similar passages; writing animations; AI colour; captions, B-roll suggestions, short clips, publishing texts and translations; stories from a topic, and the Assistant. It runs on your own account: your Claude or ChatGPT subscription (how), an API key, or a model on your own computer with LM Studio or Ollama. Kilnframe sells no credits and counts no minutes.

s: With a key of its own
x: Music and story narration: Google Gemini, or Eleven Music with an ElevenLabs key. Say Again in Voice and sound effects from text: ElevenLabs. Cloud transcription, if you turn it on: ElevenLabs, OpenAI or Google Gemini. A job that costs money on one of these asks before it starts.

For an AI job, only the text and the small frames that job needs (the transcript, your note, stills) go to the model you chose. Your videos and projects stay on your computer. With a model on your own computer, nothing leaves it. Your keys are kept in the system keychain and never sent to us. The privacy policy lists everything that leaves the app.
What an AI job changed shows in What the AI just did, a row with an Undo button. Each change is a step in History too, and Undo takes it back like any of your own.
The editor is one window in four parts: tabs at the left, the Program viewer in the middle, tabs at the right, and the timeline across the bottom.

File: new, open and save projects, export, record and more (Projects and files). Projects and the project's name, with Saved beside it: the project saves itself on every change. The frame shape, such as Horizontal 16:9. Undo and Redo, and History for every step and saved version. Shortcuts, Settings, and your licence: Trial: 14 days left or Licensed (Licence and trial). Export (Export).

Media: your recordings, shots, sounds and sequences. Transcript: what was said, word by word. Delete a word and it is cut from the video (Transcript). Animations: make an animation for a stretch, and the styles (Animations). Sound Effects: whooshes, pops and clicks to add at the playhead (Sound Effects).
The cut as it plays. Space plays and pauses. Drag the picture to move it, its corners to resize it. Overlays, Before/After and full screen are in its bar (Program).
Ten tabs, in this order: Cut, Clip, Picture, Sound, Captions, Text, Music, B-roll, Publish and Assistant. When the panel is too narrow for all of them, the rest wait under More.
Your tracks and clips in time, with the tools on its left edge and the sound meter at its right (Timeline).

s: Move tabs and save a layout
x: Right-click a tab to move it: Move to Right Panel, Move to Left Panel, Move Tab Earlier, Move Tab Later. Reset Tab Order puts them back. Drag the borders between the parts to resize them. In Settings › General: The program you are used to lays the panels out and sets the keys as Premiere Pro, Final Cut Pro, DaVinci Resolve or CapCut has them. Panel layout keeps your Workspaces: Save Layout… keeps where the panels sit, which tab is where and their sizes; Reset Layout returns the workspace in use to how it was saved.

Take the Tour, in the welcome window and the Start Window, walks you through the main panels in nine short steps. Press Esc to end it at any time. It is in Settings › General › Tour too, with Open Sample Project if you have no recording at hand.
This walk-through takes one talking-head recording from the camera to a video ready for YouTube. Each step names the button to press; the panels have pages of their own when you want more.

Install and open Kilnframe Desktop See Install. Connect an AI model In the welcome window press Connect a model. If you have a Claude or ChatGPT subscription, signing in is enough (how); otherwise enter an API key. You can also press I'll add it later in Settings: the transcript and the pause cutting work without a model. Answer the program question Which editing program are you used to? sets the shortcuts and the panels. If you like, press Take the Tour for a short walk through the editor.
Drop the file Drag your video onto Drop your video or audio here in the Start Window, or press Add Files. A project opens with the recording on the timeline.

Everything in this part happens in the Cut tab at the right. Transcribe Under 1 Transcript, press Transcribe. The speech is written down on this computer; a progress line shows how far it is. Cut the pauses and the ums Under 2 Pauses and filler words, set the slider between Gentle and Tight, then press Cut Pauses and Cut Filler Words. The length under the viewer drops at once: in our sample, 1:27 became 0:53. Clean the retakes Under 3 Retakes and what does not belong, press Clean Retakes and Asides. Your AI model finds the sentences you said twice, the false starts and the talk not meant for the viewer. Decide what it was unsure of Under 4 Unsure cuts and takes, listen and press Cut or Keep.

Choose a stretch Play to where the animation should start and press I, then to where it ends and press O. You can also select words in the transcript and choose Mark In and Out to Selection. Make it Open the Animations tab, pick a style, and press Make Animation. A note, a logo or a photo under Note and Images (optional) steers it. Approve the scenes First you see a still of each scene. Change one with Rewrite Scene; when you like them, press Approve and Create. The animation lands on its own track above your recording.
Captions Open the Captions tab, pick a Look and press Make Captions. Loudness In the Sound tab, under Effects, set Loudness to YouTube (-14 LUFS).

Open Export Press Export at the top right. Pick the size Under Size choose YouTube. High (recommended) and H.264 (plays everywhere) are right for most videos. Save it Press Export… and choose where the file goes. Every step above can be undone with Undo, or from History. More in Export and Projects and files.

Kilnframe Desktop runs on Mac, Windows and Linux. The steps are short on each; what happens on the first start is the same everywhere. Not out yet. Kilnframe Desktop comes out soon. Leave your email and we write on launch day.

System What runs it Mac Apple silicon (M1 or later). Windows Windows 10 (version 1809) or later, x64 or Arm. From the Microsoft Store, as a Beta. Linux x64 or Arm64, as an AppImage. Beta. 16 GB of memory is recommended. A graphics card is not required; when there is one (NVIDIA, AMD, Intel or Apple), exports use it and run several times faster.

Download Download the Mac version from kilnframe.com. Move it to Applications Open the downloaded file and drag Kilnframe Desktop into the Applications folder. Open it Open it from Applications. New versions arrive by themselves: the app asks before it installs one.

On Windows, Kilnframe Desktop comes only from the Microsoft Store. Find it in the Store Open the Microsoft Store and search for Kilnframe Desktop, or follow the link on kilnframe.com. Install Press Get (or Install). The Store keeps the app up to date.

On Linux, Kilnframe Desktop is one AppImage file: nothing to install. Download Download the AppImage for your computer (x64 or Arm64). Let it run Right-click the file, choose Properties, and in Permissions turn on Allow executing file as program. In a terminal, chmod +x on the file does the same. Open it Double-click the file. Your keys and your licence are kept in the system keychain. On Linux that needs a keyring service, such as GNOME Keyring or KWallet, to be running.

Kilnframe asks two things, once. First, Which editing program are you used to? Pick Premiere Pro, Final Cut Pro, DaVinci Resolve or CapCut, and the shortcuts and the places of the panels follow it. Pick None if you are new to editing. You can change it later in Settings. Then the welcome window. It shows what is needed to begin: 1. Connect an AI model and 2. Drop your recording, and how many days of the trial are left. Connect a model opens the AI settings; I'll add it later in Settings closes the window; Take the Tour walks you through the editor. Next: your first video, or how to use your Claude or ChatGPT plan.
A project is a.kiln file with a folder of its own beside it. It saves itself on every change, and keeps its earlier versions.

The File menu at the top left: New Project, Open… and Open Recent. Start Window: the window with the drop area and your Recent Projects. Save and Save As… Find Media… and Collect Project… (below). Export… and Export Frame…, Brand Kits…, Record… and Add Files… New projects go to a Kilnframe folder in your Documents unless you choose another place. Next to Home Studio.kiln sits the folder Home Studio Files: the animations, voices and pictures the app makes for the project live there. Keep the two together.
Saved beside the project's name says the last change is on disk. There is nothing to remember to press.

History in the top bar has two tabs: Steps: every change since the project was opened. Click a step to go back to it; Redo brings the later steps back. Saved versions: earlier states of the project. Recent saves are kept one by one, older ones every quarter hour. Go Back to This returns to one, and that can be undone too.

If a recording is no longer where the project left it, the clip says Missing. Find it. Open File › Find Media… and press Find… beside a missing file. When you find one, the others in the same folder are found with it. Kilnframe checks that it is the same recording before it uses it.

s: Move a project to another computer
x: File › Collect Project… copies the project file, its folder and every media file it uses into one new folder. Press Choose Folder…, tick As a zip file if you want one file, and press Collect. The open project stays as it is.
Export, at the top right, opens one window for every kind of file. The choices are read top to bottom: what, which part, its size and quality, then the options.
What: Video, GIF, Sound only or Subtitle file (SRT or WebVTT). Part: The whole timeline, or In to Out once you have set In and Out.

Size has the platforms ready: YouTube (1920×1080), YouTube Shorts, Instagram Reels and TikTok (1080×1920), as well as Original video, Project format and Custom. The buttons under it pick the resolution: Original, 720p, 1080p, 2K or 4K. A size larger than the project's is upscaled and gets no sharper; the window says so. Shorts can be at most 3 minutes long.

Quality: High (recommended), Master (archive and re-editing, large file) or Small file (sharing, messaging). Codec: H.264 (plays everywhere), HEVC / H.265 (smaller at the same quality), ProRes 422 for further editing, or ProRes 4444, which can keep a Transparent background. For a transparent export, hide V1 on the timeline so only the titles and graphics are left.
Tick the platforms under Also export (into the same folder) and each one is exported after the first, in its own size.

Hardware acceleration uses your graphics card: several times faster, with a slightly larger file. Chapters in the file writes the video's chapters into it. The chapters come from Write Publishing Texts in the Publish tab. Advanced holds a Fixed bit rate (Mbit/s). Left empty, it follows the quality.
A looping GIF without sound, at most 60 seconds long; choose its width and its frames per second. For a longer video, set In and Out around a shorter stretch and export In to Out.

Press Export… and choose where the file goes. If something must be prepared first, such as finding the person for a crop that follows them, Kilnframe asks Prepare before exporting? with the time it takes: Prepare and Export, or Export Without Them. While the export runs, Stop Export ends it. A single picture of the frame at the playhead: File › Export Frame…
Short answers, with a link where there is more.

s: Do I pay extra for the AI?
x: Not if you have a Claude or ChatGPT subscription: sign in with it and Kilnframe uses it (how). Otherwise you enter an API key and pay its provider for what you use, or run a model on your own computer for free. Kilnframe sells no credits.

s: Does it work without an AI model?
x: Yes. The transcript, cutting pauses and filler words, the timeline, colour by hand, sound and export all work without one. Finding retakes, writing animations, AI colour and the other writing jobs need a model.
No. Your videos and projects stay on your computer. Only the text and the small frames an AI job needs go to the model you chose. See How Kilnframe uses AI and the privacy policy.
The app speaks English and Turkish. The transcript is read by a speech model that knows many languages, and it tells you which one it heard. Captions can be translated into other languages.

s: What happens when the trial ends?
x: Your projects still open and you can keep editing them. Export and AI work need a licence (Licence and trial).

s: On how many computers can I use it?
x: Two. Free one with Remove This Computer in the Licence window to move the licence to another.
Yes, within 14 days, no questions asked. Write to hello@kilnframe.com.

s: Which computers does it run on?
x: Mac with Apple silicon, Windows (x64 and Arm, from the Microsoft Store) and Linux (x64 and Arm64). 16 GB of memory is recommended (Install).

s: Do I need a graphics card?
x: No. If you have one (NVIDIA, AMD, Intel or Apple), exports use it and run several times faster.

s: I edit in Premiere Pro or DaVinci Resolve. Is this for me?
x: Kilnframe Desktop is an editor of its own, and its keys and layout can follow the program you know. If you would rather stay where you are, the free, open-source Kilnframe plugin brings the animations and the music into Premiere Pro, Resolve and FilmCraft.
Pick a stretch of your video and Kilnframe writes an animation for what you say there: titles, charts, 3D scenes, hand-drawn lines. Your AI model writes the scenes; your computer draws them.

Choose a stretch Press I where it should start and O where it ends, or select words in the transcript and choose Mark In and Out to Selection. The tab shows it: Selected: 0:20 to 0:25 (5 s). Select All takes the whole cut. Pick a style Under New Animation, choose a style from the list or the gallery above it, and where the animation sits: Automatic, Full Screen or Beside the Speaker. Steer it, if you like Under Note and Images (optional), write what it should show, for example “show the price as a chart, keep our logo at the end”. Add Image… adds a logo, product shots or screenshots (up to 12); write what each one is. Make it Press Make Animation. Before you press, the tab says about how lon

With the stills shown (the default), you first see one still for each scene under Scene stills. Nothing is drawn yet. To change a scene, write what should change and press Rewrite Scene. The note changes only that scene. When you like them, press Approve and Create. The animation is drawn and placed on its own track. Discard drops the written scenes. To add a new image, discard and add it. To draw at once without the stills, tick Draw straight away, without showing the stills in Settings › AI › Animations.
Every animation made so far is listed with its time and length. A stretch that already has one can be made again: Make Again replaces it in place, on the same track.
Pick the animation clip and tick Speaker in front: you are cut out by your mask and put in front of it, so the animation passes behind you. Cut the clip with the razor to set it for each piece.

Animation styles holds 137 styles. Search them by name or description, filter them, or make your own from pictures you like. See Animation styles and your own. Animations are among the heaviest AI jobs: the model works on each scene and image separately. The tab says so before you start.
Tell the Assistant what to change, in your own words, and it does it with the app's own tools, step by step, where you can see it.

Type under What to change and press Enter (⇧ Enter starts a new line). For example: “Cut the ums in the first 30 seconds.” “Add captions and make it vertical.” “Hide the camera from 3:00 to the end.” “Put a lower third with my name at the start.” Each step it takes is listed as it goes. Stop ends it; the steps above are done. New Conversation starts again.

Some steps wait for your OK, and the list says why: a heavy job, a step that sends data off this computer, one that cannot be undone, one that changes the whole project, or a blur where you choose what it hides. Press Run, Choose in the Window or Cancel.

Undo this request takes back everything one request did, if nothing else was edited after it. Each change is also a step in History, and shows in What the AI just did with its own Undo. The Assistant needs an AI model (How Kilnframe uses AI). Assistants outside the app, such as Claude or ChatGPT, can do the same through MCP (Connect AI assistants).
B-roll is extra footage over your talk: the product you mention, the place you describe. The B-roll tab puts your shots where they show what you say.

Add your shots Add Shots adds video files you filmed or have the rights to. Let it suggest places Suggest Places asks your AI model where in the talk each shot fits. They are listed under Suggested places. Check each one Preview shows it in the viewer before it goes on the timeline. Then Add or Skip. Added shots go on their own track over the recording, and can be moved, trimmed and graded like any clip. To find a shot in a pile of footage by describing it, see Find in footage.
Captions are made from your own words, in a look you pick. Changes show in the picture at once, and the export renders them into the video.

Pick a look Under Look, click one of the ready looks. Its pictures show your own frame with a sample line. Font keeps The look's own, or takes one of yours (Add Font…). Make them Press Make Captions. With In and Out set, only that stretch gets captions; those outside it stay. Keep them current If you cut after making them, the tab says so: press Update Captions before you export. Making them again replaces your caption edits; word corrections in the transcript are kept. To move the captions, drag them in the picture.
Adjust look holds Colours (Text, Highlight, Box; Look's Own Colours puts them back), Size and Words per line.

Under Lines, click a line: its tools open under it. Change its words in place. Split at Cursor and Merge with Next. Start −0.1 s, Start +0.1 s, End −0.1 s, End +0.1 s; in a line, Alt ← → moves its start and Alt ⇧ ← → its end. Click a word to emphasise it. Emphasis style: Highlight Colour, Larger or Both. Add Emoji: shown above the line. Suggest Emphasis asks your AI model which words stand out; Emphasise Suggested takes them.

Import SRT/VTT… brings in a subtitle file you already have. It keeps the file's own times, whatever In and Out say, and replaces your caption edits. Captions sit under full-screen animations. For a subtitle file instead of burnt-in captions, export Subtitle file (Export); for other languages, see Translation and dubbing.
The Clip tab changes what you have selected: one clip, a piece of the recording, or the whole recording. Its first line says which.

Selected: the recording. The settings change the whole recording. Selected: a piece of the recording. The settings change this piece only. Or a clip by name, such as an animation, a shot or a title. For a title, Go to Text opens its words and style. With nothing selected, the controls change the whole recording.

The tab shows the sections that fit what is selected: Transform: Opacity (%), Scale (%), position, Rotation (°) and crop from each side. Reset puts it back. The same can be done by dragging in the Program viewer. Layout: Free, Picture in picture or Split screen, to put two clips together. Speed: the rate of the clip or piece, and the kind of Slow motion: Repeat frames, Blend frames or Make new frames (slower export). Fades: fade in and out, in seconds. Motion (keyframes): size and position over time, with ready moves such as Slow Push In and Pan Left. Motion is off while a layout other than Free is chosen. Colour: AI picture, looks, manual correction, curves, wheels, LUT and scopes (Colour).

Steady shaky footage (applied on export) for a shot, and Steady the shaky recording for the recording, run on this computer. Mute the clip's sound: the picture stays, its sound is heard neither while playing nor in the export. For music: Last to the End of the Video. Short music loops with smooth seams, long music is cut; either way it fades out at the end.
The Cut tab is the Automatic cut: four steps from a raw recording to a tight one. Every step can be undone, and your own cuts and the takes you chose stay.

With no In and Out, each step works on every recording (No In/Out: every recording). Set them with In at Playhead and Out at Playhead, or the I and O keys, and the buttons work only between them: Transcribe In to Out, Cut Pauses from In to Out and so on. Clear removes them.

Transcribe writes down what is said, on this computer: nothing is sent anywhere and nothing is paid. The other steps work from it. A progress line shows how far it has got and about how long is left; Stop ends it. A long recording may take a while on a slower computer. If you want it faster, Settings › AI › Transcript can send the sound to a cloud service instead (Cloud transcription). Kilnframe asks before it does. When it is done, Language heard names the language. If it is wrong, press Read the Transcript Again.

Cut Pauses cuts the silences. The slider sets how strictly, from Gentle to Tight; move it after cutting and the cut follows. Cut Filler Words cuts hesitations like “um, uh” at once. Words that may mean something, like “like, so”, are asked about in step 4. Speed up waits, for screen recordings: where nobody speaks but the screen keeps working (an install, a page loading), the moment plays 2 to 8 times as fast instead of being cut. This step runs on your computer, without a model.

s: 3 Retakes and what does not belong
x: Clean Retakes and Asides asks your AI model to find the sentences you said again, the starts you did not finish, and talk not meant for the viewer. It cuts what it is sure of and leaves the rest for step 4. This step needs a connected model (How Kilnframe uses AI).

Where the model was not sure, the cut is listed here and shows in orange in the transcript and on the timeline. Press the play button to listen around it, then Cut or Keep. Cut All and Keep All decide them all. Below, each group of retakes shows its takes. The one kept is framed; Use This Take keeps another.
Under the steps, Find Similar Passages asks your model for the places where you make the same point twice. Listen and cut the one you do not need; nothing is cut by itself.

Step Runs 1 Transcript On this computer (or a cloud service, if you choose one) 2 Pauses and filler words On this computer 3 Retakes and asides, Similar passages Your AI model 4 Unsure cuts and takes You decide
The Media tab holds everything the project uses: your recordings, the shots and sounds you add, and the project's sequences.

Recordings: the timeline is made of these. The first video or sound you drop becomes the project's recording; it is what the transcript and the automatic cut work on. Shots and sounds: extra footage, pictures, music and sounds to put over or beside the recording. Drag one onto the timeline, or add it with +. To add files, press Add Files, drop them on the tab, or click an empty place in it. Video, sound and pictures all go in.

The + under a shot opens Add to the Timeline: Over the recording, at the playhead Before the recording or After the recording for a sound: At the playhead, on A2 Right-click a file for New Project from This File and Delete. Record and Find in Footage sit at the top of the tab (Record screen and camera, Find in footage).

If you recorded your voice apart (a clip-on mic, a recorder), right-click that sound and choose Line Up with the Recording (as a Microphone). It is matched to the recording by its sound and replaces the camera's sound. The Sound tab can switch back.

Sequences lists the project's timelines. Double-click one to open it. The… beside it opens a menu with Duplicate, Vertical Copy (9:16), Square Copy (1:1), Place in Open Sequence, Rename…, a colour and Delete…. A project keeps at least one sequence. More in Sequences.
View switches between Thumbnails (small, medium or large) and a List with columns: colour label, kind, name, length, format and In use, which marks what is on the timeline.
The Music tab makes music for your video, in parts that follow its topics, and keeps it under your voice.

Choose who makes it Made with: Google Lyria (Gemini key) or Eleven Music (ElevenLabs key). Enter the key in Settings › AI; the tab says whether it is saved. Say what you want, if you like Your wish for the music (optional): a mood, an instrument, a tempo. Make it Press Make Music. Your AI model writes the plan, part by part, and the music service makes each part. Eleven Music uses your ElevenLabs credits (paid plans only), and Kilnframe asks before it does. If a part could not be made, the tab says This part got no music.; Make the Music Again tries again.

The music is lowered under the speech by itself (Under speech). If you cut after making it, its level no longer fits: press Update the Level. The music track's level and the dip under speech are in the Sound tab.

Put your own music on the music track (A3) from Media. Pick it, and in the Clip tab press Last to the End of the Video: short music loops with smooth seams, long music is cut, and either way it fades out at the end. Find Beats marks its beats to cut to (Timeline).
The Picture tab sets how your video is framed: its shape, where the crop sits, what happens behind you. The colour of each clip is in the Clip tab.
The shape is chosen in the top bar: Horizontal 16:9, Vertical 9:16 or Square 1:1. When the recording does not fit the shape, pick Crop to Fill or Fit With Bars.

Follow the person keeps the crop on you as you move, instead of Fixed. Crop position moves a fixed crop. The Person: Find the Person looks for you in each recording, for the crop that follows you and the zoom at cuts. It runs on this computer only when you ask (or when an export needs it), and is kept. Behind the speaker: As filmed, Blurred or Darkened. The person is found once; it can take a few minutes.
When a piece is cut out of one shot, Zoom in at cuts shows the next piece a little closer, so the cut looks like a change of camera angle. Left empty, 8 to 12 % is chosen.

The same tab holds Camera (tutorials), for a camera paired with a screen recording (Screen tutorials), and Virtual multicam, which makes a close frame for each person in a wide shot and cuts to whoever speaks (Multicam and speakers). Default slow motion sets how slowed footage is filled in, for every clip that does not set its own.
Colour belongs to each clip and piece: select one and grade it in the Clip tab. Go to Colour takes you there (Colour). Everything here shows live in the viewer and is used on export.
Program shows the cut as it will be exported. Its bar holds playback, the view tools and full screen; the picture itself can be moved, resized and cropped by hand.

Space plays and pauses. The buttons, from the left: the time, Go to start, Previous edit point, play, Next edit point, Go to end, loop, and In and Out. J, K and L play backwards, stop and play forwards; I and O set In and Out. Playback quality: Smooth plays a phone's 4K and HEVC videos from a light copy; Full quality plays the file itself, for fast computers. The export is always full quality.

The Overlays button shows lines and frames that help you place things. They are never in the export. Centre cross and Rule of thirds. Title and action safe: where text is safe on every screen. Shorts, Reels and TikTok buttons: where those apps put their buttons over a vertical video. Other shapes (9:16, 1:1, 4:5): where a vertical or square copy would crop, following the person. Rulers and guides: drag from a ruler to add a guide line, drag it back to remove it. ⌘ ' (Ctrl ') hides or shows them all.

Before/After shows the picture without your colour work. Its menu has Before, After, Split view (both side by side, split by a line) and Off. Clips over the recording, such as titles, show as they are.

s: Move, resize and crop in the picture
x: Click the picture to pick the clip under the pointer. Then: drag it to move it; drag a corner to resize it; drag an edge to crop it; drag the circle above it to turn it. It snaps into place as you drag; hold Alt to drag freely, Shift to keep the centre. On a title or a graphic the edges resize it too, keeping its shape, and Alt crops it. The Clip tab sets exact numbers.

s: Full screen and a second screen
x: The full screen button shows the viewer alone on the screen (Viewer Full Screen, ⇧ ⌘ F); Esc leaves. Its menu offers Picture on the other screen when a second screen is connected.
The camera button saves the frame at the playhead as a picture (Export Frame, ⇧ ⌘ E).
The Publish tab gets the video ready to post: short clips from it, the words that go with it, and other languages.

Find Short Clips edits short videos of 20 to 60 seconds out of the long one, for Shorts, Reels and TikTok. Each comes with a score for how well it holds a viewer on its own. Save as Sequence makes it a tall sequence of the project, to open, edit and export. See Short clips.

Write Publishing Texts asks your AI model for: Title 1, Title 2 and Title 3: three, ready for YouTube's own A/B test; Description With Chapters: chapter times follow the cut; Tags; Cover ideas: a prompt for the image model you like (Copy Prompt, Copy Vertical Prompt), the words to put on it, and a frame of the video for it: Take Frame Here takes the frame at the playhead, Save Frame saves it. Copy beside each puts it on the clipboard. Names in the transcript's glossary are spelled as you keep them. The chapters can also go into the exported file (Export).
Under Translation, pick Languages and press Translate: your AI model translates the cut's speech into subtitles for each language. Dub has them read by a voice. See Translation and dubbing.
Whooshes, pops, clicks and dings, ready to drop on the timeline. The built-in sounds are made by Kilnframe itself.

Type in Search: whoosh, pop, ding…, or pick a Category: Whoosh, Swoosh, Riser, Pop, Click and tick, Ding and chime, Impact and hit, Glitch, Typing and more. Play listens to it; Space plays the one you picked. Add at Playhead puts it on the timeline where the playhead is, or press Enter. You can also drag a sound onto a sound track.
More Sounds downloads about 200 real recordings that anyone may use (CC0). It happens only when you press the button. Sound Credits lists where they come from; they need no credit in your video.

s: Make a sound from a text
x: Under Make a Sound Effect from Text, describe the sound, for example “a heavy wooden door creaks open”, set a Length (seconds) or leave it to ElevenLabs, and press Make. The new sound goes to the top of the list, under Made by you. This needs an ElevenLabs API key (Settings › AI). The text is sent to ElevenLabs and the sound uses your ElevenLabs credits; Kilnframe asks once before the first one. Sounds placed from here do not dip under the speech; your own music and sounds do (Sound and Mixer).
The Sound tab cleans the voice, sets it to the right loudness and keeps the music under it. Every setting is heard while playing as the export makes it.

One fader for each track: Speech, Effects, Music, and Main Out for the whole mix, with meters while playing. A fader lowers or raises its track all through; at the foot the track is off. Double-click a fader (or Alt and a click) to set it back to 0 dB.

Effects work on a whole track (Track effect) or on one clip or piece of the speech (Clip effect); a clip's own effects run before its track's. Effects on switches them all. Noise Reduction: takes away the hum of the room. Voice isolation (AI): keeps the speech and drops the rest. It runs on this computer; Get the Voice Model (16 MB) downloads its model once, then Clean the Voice and Strength. Voice: Presence, Less mud, Less boom, De-ess and Gate quiet parts. Reduce room echo: set the amount, then Reduce Echo. It runs on this computer.
Loudness: YouTube (-14 LUFS), Podcast (-16 LUFS) or Leave As Is. The speech is measured and brought to that level. Peak Level: the loudest the mix may get. Fuller voice (broadcast).

Dip my music and sounds under the speech: while you speak, your own music and sounds go down by the Dip Amount, and come back up smoothly after it over the Fade. Music made by the app and effects from the Sound Effects library do not dip.

Voice-over: ● Start Recording records from your microphone from the playhead, on A2; the video plays silent meanwhile. Text to speech: type the Text to read, pick a Voice and press Read Aloud. It goes on A2 at the playhead. Gemini voices need a Gemini key, ElevenLabs voices an ElevenLabs key.
A microphone recorded apart is matched to the recording by its sound and replaces the camera's: Add Microphone Recording…. Back to Camera Sound undoes it.

The Text tab makes titles and graphics: a name and role, a headline, a quote, an arrow, a Subscribe button. Each goes on the top track at the playhead, for 4 seconds; drag its edges on the timeline to change that.

Start from a template, or not Templates: Built in ones such as Name that slides in, Headline typed on, Quote or Chapter card, and Yours. Pick its kind Kind: Headline, Lower third (name and role), Words in a box, Corner tag, Callout (a box with a pointer), Quote, Subscribe button, Chapter card or Numbered list. Write it Text, and a second line where the kind has one (a role, who said it, the chapter number). Place: Top, Middle or Bottom; Size, Colour and Font. Choose how it moves Comes in: at once, fade in, fade up, pop, slide in from the left, type on letter by letter, word by word. Goes out: at once, fade out, fade down, pop, slide out to the left. Add it Add at the Playhead. Style adds an

Shapes and stickers: an Arrow, a Line, a Box, an Ellipse, a Highlight box, an Emoji, or a Sticker such as Subscribe button, Like or Bell. Set its colour, Line thickness or Size, and press Add at the Playhead. It goes in the middle of the frame; drag it in the viewer to place it. Your own fonts and brand colours can come from a brand kit (Brand kits and fonts).
The timeline holds your recording and everything placed over and under it. The tools sit on its left edge, the zoom and the snapping above it, the sound meter at its right.

V1: your recording, cut into pieces by the automatic cut and by you. V2 and up: what goes over it: shots, titles, animations, pictures. Higher tracks cover lower ones. V0 Background: under the recording, for a background behind a picture made smaller. A1: the speech. A2: sound effects. A3: music. Each track has buttons to hide, mute, solo and lock it; sound tracks have fx for their effects. The + above the track names adds a track (Add Video Track, Add Audio Track).

The keys below are Kilnframe's own; with another program's keys chosen in Settings, they follow that program. Tool Key What it does Select V Pick a piece or a clip; drag a clip to move it, to another track too. Razor C Cut a clip or the recording where you click. Hand H Drag the timeline along. Pen P Click a sound track to add a volume point. Rate Stretch R Drag an edge: longer plays slower, shorter plays faster; the sound keeps its pitch. Roll T Drag the joint between two pieces: one gets longer as the other gets shorter. Slip Y Show an earlier or later part of a clip, in the same place and length. Track Select Forward A Pick everything from where you click on, to move it all together. Text

Right-click a clip for, among others: Speed…, Reverse, Freeze Frame, Split at Scene Changes, Replace With…, Copy Settings and Paste Settings, Make Compound Clip, Show in Media and Delete and Close the Gap (Ripple Delete). An item that does not apply to the clip is greyed, with the reason beside it.
At a cut, Add Cross Dissolve (⌘ D) or Add Dip to Black (⇧ ⌘ D). Cross Dissolve at Every Cut does them all at once, Remove All Transitions takes them away. On sound, Add Sound Crossfade.

M adds a marker at the playhead; ⇧ M goes to the next one. A marker can be orange, blue, green, red or purple and can carry a note. Find Beats marks the beats of a music clip, so you can cut to them. Close All Gaps pulls the clips together where empty space is left.
Follow the playhead, above the tracks: Page by page turns the view a page at a time, Smooth keeps the playhead still and moves the clips under it, Off leaves the view where it is.
The Transcript tab is your recording as text. What you delete here is cut from the video; what you bring back returns.

Cut: select one or more words and press Delete. They stay in the text, struck out, and the video jumps over them. Bring back: click a struck-out word. Move: drag selected words to another place to change the order of what you say. Back to Recording Order on the timeline undoes the moves. The transcript appears once the recording is transcribed in the Cut tab. If only part of it was read, Transcribe the Rest reads the remainder.

Hold the pointer over a struck-out word to see why it went: Pause, Filler word, Retake, False start, Off topic or Cut by you. Words underlined in orange are the ones the model was not sure of: decide them in step 4 of the Cut tab.

Select words and right-click them: Cut: the same as Delete. Mark In and Out to Selection: sets In and Out around the words, for an animation, a caption range or an export of that part. Correct Words…: fix a word that was heard wrong. The text changes, the sound stays. Tick Add to glossary and the name is spelled right in captions, translations and the publishing texts. Bring Back Heard Words undoes it. Say Again in Voice…: type what you should have said, and it is read again in your own voice (needs an ElevenLabs key). Glossary, at the top of the tab, keeps names and brands spelled exactly as you write them.
Press ⌘ F (Ctrl F on Windows and Linux) for Find in the transcript. Previous and Next step through the matches.

In the Cut tab, Find Similar Passages asks your AI model for the places where you make the same point twice. They are marked in colour in the transcript; listen and cut the one you do not need. Nothing is cut by itself.
Under the title, Language heard names the language the speech was read in. If it is wrong, read the transcript again from the Cut tab.

Your speech is transcribed on your own computer. The pauses, the ums and the sentences you said twice go; what it is unsure about, it asks you. Transcribe The speech is written down on this computer. No internet needed. Cut Pauses, from Gentle to Tight The silences go in one click, as tight as you like. Cut Filler Words “Um” and “uh” are cut; words that may mean something are asked about. Clean Retakes and Asides Your AI model finds the sentences you said again and the talk not meant for the viewer. Unsure cuts and takes Where it is not sure, you decide: Cut or Keep, and Use This Take. Find Similar Passages Shows where you made the same point twice. In and Out Cut only the stretch you choose

s: Edit the video like a text.
x: Delete a word in the transcript and it is cut from the video. Click it and it comes back. Transcript Delete, bring back and move words; hold the pointer over a cut word to see why it went. Correct Words… and Glossary Fix a name that was heard wrong; captions, translations and chapters use the right spelling. Say Again in Voice… Type the word you said wrong, and it is read again in your own voice. Find in the transcript Find a phrase and go to it. Move sentences, Back to Recording Order Change the order of what you say, in the text.

Pick a stretch and Kilnframe writes scenes for what you are talking about: titles, charts, 3D, hand-drawn lines, kinetic type. Make Animation Scenes made for the stretch you chose, timed to the frame. Note and Images (optional) Steer it with a note, your logo or a photo. Scene stills: Rewrite Scene, Approve and Create See each scene before it is drawn, and change the ones you want. 137 animation styles, 37 of them 3D Filter by kind, mood, colour and what they suit. Each style comes with its own sounds. Your Own Style Extract a style from pictures you like. Speaker in front The animation passes behind you.

One click for good skin tones and a bright picture; every control by hand when you want it. Fix with AI, Fix Skin Tone, Rescue Dark Footage, Match a Reference… AI colour that you can see, change and undo. Match Recordings Two cameras made to look alike. Colour look and Look strength Ready looks such as Cinematic, as strong as you like. Basic correction, Colour curves, Colour wheels, LUT Every setting by hand. Waveform, RGB parade, Vectorscope Measure the colour while you set it. Before/After, Split view See what a change did, side by side. Skin smoothing, Sharpen, Dark edges The last touches. Framing and background: Follow the person, Behind the speaker The speaker stays in frame, even in a

A clean voice at the right loudness, with music that steps back while you talk. Noise Reduction Takes away the hum of the room. Voice isolation (AI) Keeps the speech and drops the background, on this computer. Reduce room echo Less echo from an empty room. Loudness: YouTube (-14 LUFS), Podcast (-16 LUFS) The right level for the platform, in one choice. Ducking Your music goes down while you speak. Presence, Less mud, De-ess, Gate quiet parts A broadcast voice, track by track or clip by clip. Mixer Speech, effects, music and the main out, with meters. Make Music Music made for the parts of your video, with a Gemini or ElevenLabs key. Sound Effects, Make a Sound Effect from Text Whoosh, pop, c

Record your screen and your camera without leaving the app; your face goes in the corner and the picture zooms to where you work. Record Screen and Camera… Screen, camera and microphone, recorded in the app. Camera: In a corner, Side by side, Face full screen The camera and the screen line up by their sound; your face sits in the corner. Camera sections: This section, From here on Move the camera as the lesson goes on. Screen zoom: Find Activity and Zoom Zooms in where you type and click. Speed up waits Installs and loading play faster instead of being cut. Mouse highlight, Add Click Sounds The pointer and the clicks are seen and heard. Shapes and stickers Arrows, highlight boxes, a Subscrib

Cameras line up by their sound, and the cut follows whoever is speaking. Add Cameras and Speakers' Microphones… Cameras and microphones lined up by their sound. Follow Who Speaks The cut switches to the camera of the person speaking. Angles Every angle in the viewer at once; pick one with a number key. Virtual multicam: Frame Whoever Speaks Close-ups made from a single wide shot.

Captions in a click, in a look you pick, and titles that come in and go out with motion. Make Captions, Look Captions from your words, in a ready look. Lines: Split at Cursor, Merge with Next Fix a line, its timing and its emphasis. Emphasis, Emoji Colour the word that matters, add an emoji. Import SRT/VTT… Bring the captions you already have. Text templates: Headline, Lower third, Chapter card… Titles with their own way in and out. Brand kits Intro, outro, colours, fonts and caption look, ready in every project. Add Font… Use your own fonts.

Shorts from the strongest moments, a title, description and chapters for each video, and translations. Find Short Clips Vertical clips from a long video that hold up on their own. Save as Sequence, Vertical Copy (9:16) Edit a short as a sequence of its own. Write Publishing Texts Titles, a description with chapters, tags and cover ideas. Translation, Dub Captions in other languages, read aloud if you like. Make a Story From a Topic No recording? A narrated draft from a topic.

The tools, tracks and keys of the program you are used to, under all of the above. Select, Razor, Rate Stretch, Roll, Slip, Pen, Text The editing tools you know, with their keys. Add Video Track, Lock, Mute As many tracks as you need. Add Cross Dissolve, Add Dip to Black Transitions, and crossfades for sound. Motion and keyframes Animate size, place, opacity, rotation and crop. Speed…, Reverse, Freeze Frame, Slow motion Speed changes, smooth slow motion too. Green screen Take away the background colour. Blur faces and areas Pick a face; the blur follows it. Picture in picture, Split screen Any two clips side by side. Adjustment layer One colour change over many clips. Make Compound Clip, Seq

The platform's size ready, several platforms at once, with your graphics card. Size: YouTube, YouTube Shorts, Instagram Reels, TikTok The platform's size, ready. Codec: H.264, HEVC / H.265, ProRes; Transparent background For sharing, for the archive, or to keep editing. Also export Several platforms in one go. Subtitle file, Chapters in the file Ready to upload to YouTube. GIF, Export Frame… A short loop or a single frame. Hardware acceleration Fast on NVIDIA, AMD, Intel and Apple.

s: Your own AI, the Assistant and MCP.
x: The AI work runs on your own account. No credits to buy from us. Claude Plan, ChatGPT Plan Your subscription covers it; nothing extra to pay. API Key, LM Studio, Ollama With a key, or entirely on your computer with a local model. Assistant Ask for a change in your own words; it does it step by step. What the AI just did Every AI step is shown, and Undo takes it back. Connect AI assistants (MCP) Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and Codex can edit your project.

s: Safe, and set up your way.
x: Nothing is lost, nothing heavy starts without asking, and the keys are the ones you know. Saved by itself, History: Steps, Saved versions No step is lost; go back to an earlier version. Find Media…, Collect Project… Find moved files; gather a project into one folder. The program you are used to: Premiere Pro, Final Cut Pro, DaVinci Resolve, CapCut The layout and the keys you know. Workspaces Move the panels and keep your layout. Keyboard shortcuts, Edit Shortcuts Change any key. Running work, Asked work Heavy work asks before it starts and can be stopped at any time.

Your videos stay on your computer: transcription, cutting and export run on your machine, and AI work sends only the text and frames a job needs to the model you choose.
